claims.title: Dutch found Fort Zeelandia
claims.summary: The Dutch East India Company establishes a fortified trading base, Fort Zeelandia, on the southwestern coast near present-day Tainan, beginning roughly four decades of Dutch commercial rule over parts of the island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1624-dutch-found-fort-zeelandia, claim TL:TWN:event:1624:dutch-found-fort-zeelandia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish settle the northern coast
claims.summary: Spanish forces from the Philippines occupy northern Taiwan, building forts at Keelung and Tamsui in response to the Dutch presence in the south.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1626-spanish-settle-the-northern-coast, claim TL:TWN:event:1626:spanish-settle-the-northern-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dutch expel the Spanish
claims.summary: A Dutch expedition drives the Spanish from their northern outposts, leaving the Dutch East India Company as the dominant European power on the island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1642-dutch-expel-the-spanish, claim TL:TWN:event:1642:dutch-expel-the-spanish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Koxinga expels the Dutch
claims.summary: After a siege begun in 1661, the Ming-loyalist commander Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) forces the surrender of Fort Zeelandia, ending Dutch rule and founding the Zheng (Tungning) regime on Taiwan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1662-koxinga-expels-the-dutch, claim TL:TWN:event:1662:koxinga-expels-the-dutch, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Qing conquest of the Zheng regime
claims.summary: A Qing fleet defeats the Zheng (Tungning) forces, ending the Ming-loyalist kingdom; Taiwan is annexed the following year and attached to Fujian province as a prefecture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1683-qing-conquest-of-the-zheng-regime, claim TL:TWN:event:1683:qing-conquest-of-the-zheng-regime, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Taiwan made a Qing province
claims.summary: The Qing government raises Taiwan to the status of a separate province, with Liu Mingchuan as reforming first governor promoting railways and modernisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1885-taiwan-made-a-qing-province, claim TL:TWN:event:1885:taiwan-made-a-qing-province, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Shimonoseki cedes Taiwan to Japan
claims.summary: Ending the First Sino-Japanese War, the treaty obliges the Qing empire to cede Taiwan and the Pescadores to Japan, beginning fifty years of Japanese colonial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1895-treaty-of-shimonoseki-cedes-taiwan-to-japan, claim TL:TWN:event:1895:treaty-of-shimonoseki-cedes-taiwan-to-japan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese colonial administration
claims.summary: Japan develops Taiwan with railways, ports, public health and expanded agriculture while suppressing resistance and, from the late 1930s, pursuing intensive assimilation campaigns.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1895-japanese-colonial-administration, claim TL:TWN:event:1895:japanese-colonial-administration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ROC takes over Taiwan
claims.summary: After Japan's surrender, the Republic of China under the Nationalists (Kuomintang) takes over the administration of Taiwan from Japan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1945-roc-takes-over-taiwan, claim TL:TWN:event:1945:roc-takes-over-taiwan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: February 28 Incident
claims.summary: Protests against Nationalist rule, triggered by a violent monopoly-enforcement episode in Taipei, are crushed by troops; thousands are killed, beginning the long repression known as the White Terror.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1947-february-28-incident, claim TL:TWN:event:1947:february-28-incident, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
claims.summary: Having defeated the Nationalists in the Chinese Civil War, Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China on the mainland; Chiang and his forces withdraw toward Taiwan.

sources.label: The Chinese Revolution of 1949
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1949-people-s-republic-of-china-proclaimed, claim TL:TWN:event:1949:people-s-republic-of-china-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ROC government relocates to Taiwan
claims.summary: Chiang Kai-shek's Republic of China central government relocates to Taipei after defeat in the civil war, founding the present self-governing polity on the island; this was not a declaration of independence.

sources.label: The Chinese Revolution of 1949
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1949-roc-government-relocates-to-taiwan, claim TL:TWN:event:1949:roc-government-relocates-to-taiwan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN seat transferred to the PRC
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly votes to seat the People's Republic of China in China's place at the United Nations; the ROC's representatives lose the seat. The resolution does not address Taiwan's sovereignty.

sources.label: Rapprochement with China, 1972
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Shanghai Communiqué
claims.summary: During President Nixon's visit to China, the United States and the PRC issue the Shanghai Communiqué; the U.S. acknowledges the position that there is but one China, beginning normalisation.

sources.label: Rapprochement with China, 1972
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1972-shanghai-communique, claim TL:TWN:event:1972:shanghai-communique, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: U.S. switches recognition to the PRC
claims.summary: The United States establishes formal diplomatic relations with the PRC as the sole legal government of China and ends recognition of the ROC; Congress passes the Taiwan Relations Act to sustain unofficial ties.

sources.label: China Policy (Normalization of Relations, 1979)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1979-u-s-switches-recognition-to-the-prc, claim TL:TWN:event:1979:u-s-switches-recognition-to-the-prc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: National Palace Museum opens in Taipei
claims.summary: A permanent home opens in Taipei for a vast collection of Chinese imperial art and antiquities, much of it relocated from the mainland around 1948 to 1949.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1965-national-palace-museum-opens-in-taipei, claim TL:TWN:event:1965:national-palace-museum-opens-in-taipei, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Martial law lifted
claims.summary: President Lee Teng-hui ends nearly four decades of martial law and the ban on travel to the mainland, opening the way to democratic reform.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1987-martial-law-lifted, claim TL:TWN:event:1987:martial-law-lifted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First direct presidential election
claims.summary: Lee Teng-hui wins Taiwan's first direct, popular presidential election, becoming its first democratically elected president and completing the democratic transition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Taiwan: An Austronesian island colonised in turn by Dutch, Spanish, Ming-loyalist, Qing and Japanese hands, and now the seat of a self-governing polity at the centre of an unresolved cross-strait dispute.", terralore.co/country/TWN/chronicle#ev-1996-first-direct-presidential-election, claim TL:TWN:event:1996:first-direct-presidential-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ongoing cross-strait dispute
claims.summary: Into 2026 the dispute remains unresolved: the ROC governs Taiwan while the PRC claims it as a province without controlling it, and no peace treaty has settled the question.
